visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) Two young girls with pigtails are seated at a wooden dining table in a bright, modern kitchen. One child wears a blue and red tank top, while the other wears a pink floral dress. They interact with an off-screen adult, exhibiting expressive facial movements and wide smiles. The setting features light wood furniture and a glimpse of a clean kitchen counter in the background. (2) A woman's hands appear, pouring a white powder from a small bowl into a light-colored pot filled with water resting on the table. The girls lean forward with curiosity, their hands resting on the table surface. A woman in a grey graphic t-shirt helps one of the girls stir the white liquid with a large spoon. (3) Three bowls containing diced kiwi, blueberries, and watermelon are placed on the table. The girls begin picking up the fruit pieces and placing them into small, transparent triangular plastic bags. One girl in a pink dress is shown hesitating and eventually eating a piece of watermelon rather than bagging it, with a playful, mischievous expression. (4) An adult uses a black ladle to carefully pour a clear liquid from the pot into the plastic bags already filled with fruit. The children watch the process closely. Later, the group claps their hands together over a tray filled with multiple sealed jelly bags, signaling a transition in the preparation process. (5) The girls are shown eating the finished, set fruit jelly from metal and ceramic bowls. One child has changed into a red t-shirt. They use small forks and spoons to scoop the translucent jelly. Finally, a slightly older girl in a beige sweater is seen tasting the same fruit jelly and nodding with a satisfied smile.

The BGM maintains a steady, cheerful rhythm. (3) The rhythmic sound of fruit being dropped into plastic bags creates small percussive thuds. A child's voice chirps with delight while naming the fruits. The adult voice remains calm and instructional, guiding the activity. (4) A glugging sound effect mimics the pouring of liquid, followed by a loud, synchronized hand-clapping sound that serves as an editing transition. The children's vocal arousal increases as they anticipate the results. (5) Sounds of spoons and forks clicking against metal bowls are prominent. The toddlers make soft chewing noises and express 'yummy' through rising intonations. The older sister's voice enters with a clear, happy timbre. The BGM concludes with a short, bright melodic flourish.
